label: MiniMax Music 3 CUDA music generator
summary: Use MiniMax Music 3 through an explicitly operated CUDA sidecar for complete structured songs, while preserving a local EPRS fallback on unsupported hardware.

handoffs.label: Generate a structured song through MiniMax Music 3
handoffs.intent: Send tagged lyrics and a Music 3 Structured Caption to a local or remote CUDA sidecar, then return a new lossless WAV and exact provenance.
inputs: Tagged lyrics with section labels such as [Verse], [Chorus], [Bridge], and [Outro]
A Structured Caption covering metadata, vocals, arrangement, groove, bass, and production
An explicitly operated CUDA sidecar endpoint, seed, output path, and model license note
A separate EPRS fallback plan when the sidecar is unavailable
outputs: A new 32 kHz stereo WAV from the sidecar
A manifest recording lyrics, structured caption, endpoint, seed, response probe, checksum, and MiniMax license
A local EPRS mix/master handoff with the original generated WAV preserved
steps: Read the current MiniMax Music 3 model card and Community License; do not download the 32 GB checkpoint on unsupported hardware.
Start or verify an explicitly operated CUDA sidecar with the official MiniMax Music 3 endpoint contract.
Run `python3 scripts/minimax_music3_runner.py` with tagged lyrics, instructions, a new WAV path, and a deterministic seed.
Inspect the returned WAV, preserve the manifest, and bring it into EPRS only as a source stem; do not silently replace local tools.
Apply EPRS mixing/mastering and retain the required MiniMax-Music3 disclosure for any public machine-generated release.
verification: Confirm the sidecar response is a non-empty WAV with the expected sample rate, channels, duration, and checksum.
Confirm the endpoint is intentional and credentials are not present in lyrics, manifests, logs, or public metadata.
Confirm the exact model license and public disclosure requirement are preserved with the release evidence.
Compare the MiniMax render against a local EPRS fallback before choosing the final musical direction.

preserve: The tagged lyrics, Structured Caption, model revision, seed, endpoint, generated WAV, checksum, and license evidence
The distinction between sidecar-generated audio and local EPRS authored arrangement, processing, and release decisions
avoid: Downloading or attempting to load the full checkpoint on unsupported hardware, exposing API credentials, hiding machine-generation disclosure, or presenting generated audio as a human performance
Assuming a model license clears lyrics, samples, voices, or other user-supplied material
